note: Verified, sourced league history for the post-draft recap. Machine-readable twin of data/LEAGUE-HISTORY.md — same facts, same sources, same confidence marks. Read the Markdown for the reasoning; read this for the values.
compiledFor: The 2026 post-draft AI recap. Every entry is intended to be safe to build a joke on.
howToRead: Every factual entry carries `source` and `confidence`. Nothing here is asserted without one.
`confidence: verified` means a primary source in this repo says it in terms, or two independent sources in this repo agree.
`confidence: derived` means it was computed from repo data by a stated method, and `scripts/verify-league-history.mjs` re-computes it on demand.
`confidence: inferred` means it follows from repo data by an argument that is stated, not from a source that says it outright. Treat as probably true; do not read it aloud as a hard number.
`confidence: unverified` appears only in the `unverified` block at the foot of this file. Nothing in that block may be stated as fact in a blurb.
MANAGERS ARE KEYED BY SHORT NAME. Never match on a first name — four managers share one and two of them are called Scott. See `managers` and `identityTrap`.

identityTrap.why: Four of the ten managers share a first name with another manager, and 'Scott' and 'Kyle' are each simultaneously a legitimate short name for one man AND the first name of a different one. A first-name match does not fail loudly; it silently resolves to the wrong franchise. A joke landed on the wrong Scott, in a room containing both Scotts, is worse than no joke.
identityTrap.rule: Match on the short name from data/managers.json, or on a stable id. Never on a first name.

keeperRules.notRequiredToFill: Nobody is required to fill both slots. Joe deliberately kept one.
keeperRules.costRoundRule: Cost round = the player's previous-season draft round minus one. A free-agent acquisition costs the 9th round.
keeperRules.tenure: Three consecutive seasons total: the acquisition season plus two keeper seasons. Written 'N of 3' in the keeper sheets, where year 1 is the season the player was acquired.
keeperRules.tradeResetsClock: A trade restarts a player's keeper eligibility with his new team, but the player retains his previous season's draft-round value. Clock resets; cost basis carries.
keeperRules.roundOneIneligible: A player who occupied a round-1 slot last season can never be kept — pricing him would need a round 0. Every first-round pick is a one-year rental, permanently. Ruled Aug 26 2026; codifies existing practice.
keeperRules.sourceOddity: The league's keeper rules are stated most clearly in the recitals of a private contract between two managers. This app reads the rules out of that contract.

draftOrder2026.mechanic: A SLOT AUCTION conducted in reverse-standings order. Finishing position decides WHEN you choose, not WHAT you get. The team that finished last chooses any slot it likes; the champion chooses last from what is left.
draftOrder2026.workedExample: Colin finished 3rd and chose the 10th slot, because slot 10 owns the turn — picks 10 and 11 back to back. Greg and Stefan chose after him, landing at 9 and 8.
draftOrder2026.source: data/DECISIONS.md, 'How the order is actually set'; ROADMAP.md, commissioner quote

standings2025.method: Derived from the slot-auction quote. Choosing order is worst-first; Colin chose before Greg, who chose before Stefan, so Stefan finished ahead of Greg, who finished ahead of Colin. Colin states he finished 3rd, which fixes the other two at 2nd and 1st.

But when you win the ship you don't get to pick where you draft' (R10 p92), and Kyle says of Joe Mixon 'He won you a title last year, show some respect' (R3 p30) — both of which put a title on Stefan for the 2023 season as well.
standings2025.caution: The finishing positions of the other seven franchises are NOT recorded anywhere in this repo. Do not invent a standings table.

nacuaAgreement.headline: Two managers wrote a real contract for a fantasy football trade, gave one of them a free option on the other man's first-round pick, and the one who drafted it is a lawyer.

primarySource.title: TRADE AGREEMENT
primarySource.length: Two pages, the second of which is a standalone signature page.
primarySource.note: The PDF was copied into the repository from the operator's machine on 2026-08-28 so the source is durable. Before that, every quotation of it in this repo was second-hand through data/DECISIONS.md.

form.fact: It has WHEREAS recitals, a 'NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants, terms, and conditions' clause, defined terms in quotation marks, a 'For the avoidance of doubt' sentence, '{Remainder of page intentionally left blank; signature page follows}', and 'IN WITNESS WHEREOF'. It carries a law-firm document control number.

typo.fact: Clause 2 defines the deal as 'the "Continent 2026 Trade"' — missing the g. The defined term is therefore 'Continent 2026 Trade', and every later reference in the document calls it the 'Contingent 2026 Trade', which the document never defines.
typo.whyFunny: A lawyer's contract with a typo in its own defined term, and then a defined term he never uses again.

quotableVerbatim: WHEREAS, JJ and DHB are each teams competing in that certain fantasy football league known as The Ultimate Keeper League (the "League");

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants, terms, and conditions set forth in this Agreement, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

On the day before the 2026 League Draft, as long as Nacua is not projected by a majority of media outlets to miss six (6) weeks or more of the 2026 season due to injury (a "Nacua Injury"), DHB and JJ agree to consummate the following trade (the "Continent 2026 Trade"):

In the event of a Nacua Injury, DHB shall have the option prior to the 2026 League Draft to either (i) consummate the Contingent 2026 Trade, or (ii) cancel the Contingent 2026 Trade, with DHB retaining the picks exchanged in the 2025 Trade and JJ retaining Nacua.
For the avoidance of doubt, Nacua shall retain his 2026 League Draft 11th round draft Keeper eligibility whether or not the Contingent 2026 Trade is consummated.
{Remainder of page intentionally left blank; signature page follows}

clause2_contingentTrade.trigger: To be consummated on the day before the 2026 League Draft — Friday 2026-08-28 — as long as there is no "Nacua Injury".
clause2_contingentTrade.nacuaInjuryDefinition: Nacua being "projected by a majority of media outlets to miss six (6) weeks or more of the 2026 season due to injury".

theOption.text: In the event of a Nacua Injury, DHB shall have the option prior to the 2026 League Draft to either (i) consummate the Contingent 2026 Trade, or (ii) cancel the Contingent 2026 Trade, with DHB retaining the picks exchanged in the 2025 Trade and JJ retaining Nacua.
theOption.holder: DHB — Scott Johnston. JJ holds no corresponding election in any branch.

theAsymmetry.statement: The option is one-directional and it is written that way in the document, not inferred from it.

branches.whatHappens: Both parties 'agree to consummate' — it is mandatory on both sides. Scott takes Nacua back at an R11 keeper price; Greg gets his 2026 1st and 2027 3rd returned.
Scott takes an injured Nacua anyway and returns Greg's 2026 1st and 2027 3rd.
Scott KEEPS Greg's 2026 1st, 2026 3rd and 2027 3rd, plus Monangai. Greg is left holding an injured Nacua.

theAsymmetry.plainEnglish: Healthy Nacua: Scott gets the receiver. Injured Nacua: Scott gets to keep Greg's first-round pick instead. There is no branch in which Scott has to accept an outcome he did not choose, and no branch in which Greg gets to choose anything.

optionPricing.fact: The agreement identifies no separate consideration for the option. It is granted inside the same blanket 'other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged' recital that covers the whole document.
optionPricing.howToPhraseIt: Say the document allocates no distinct price to the option. Do NOT say Scott 'paid nothing at all' for the trade — he sent real players and picks. The point is narrower and stronger: the protection itself is free.

correctionToTheOralAccount.theClaim: The commissioner's recollection, relayed 2026-08-28: "they made a rule where, if Puca got hurt, they could revert the trade, and it wouldn't be keeper-eligible."
correctionToTheOralAccount.whatTheDocumentActuallySays: The opposite, in terms: "For the avoidance of doubt, Nacua shall retain his 2026 League Draft 11th round draft Keeper eligibility whether or not the Contingent 2026 Trade is consummated." The injury clause governs WHO HOLDS HIM, not whether he is keepable. Eligibility is preserved in every branch.
correctionToTheOralAccount.whyThisMatters: This is the one detail that would let Scott dismantle a roast on a technicality. Do not use the 'not keeper-eligible' version. The written version is worse for him anyway: they did not merely reserve a revert, they wrote a clause specifically ensuring the cheap keeper price survived either outcome.

netEffectOfBothLegs.method: Clause 1 minus clause 2, then checked pick-by-pick against the live 2026 board.

scott.nacua: Round trip — starts Scott's, ends Scott's, with a reset keeper clock in transit.

greg.nacua: Held from 2025-11-12 through the end of the 2025 season, then returned.

netEffectOfBothLegs.summary: Scott turned Derrick Henry and a 16th-round pick into Kyle Monangai and a 3rd-round pick, and got Nacua back. Greg paid Monangai and a 3rd-round pick, received a 16th-round pick, and lent his first-round pick as collateral for nine months.

gregsPermanentReturn.fact: Once the contingent leg fires, Greg's permanent return on the whole agreement is Derrick Henry plus Scott's 2026 16th-round pick — and Derrick Henry is keeper-ineligible, priced to round 0, so Greg loses him to the 2026 draft pool as well.

gregsRealMotive.fact: Nov 12 2025 falls in week 11 of a season whose regular season runs to week 14 and whose playoffs run weeks 15–17. Greg bought Nacua and Derrick Henry for the run-in, and by the slot-auction derivation he finished 2nd. He was not fleeced in a vacuum; he bought a title run and came second.
gregsRealMotive.caution: The 2nd-place finish is derived from the draft-order auction, not from a standings table. See league.standings2025.

netEffectOfBothLegs.boardVerification: Every leg checks out against the live board: Scott holds Greg's R3, Greg holds Scott's R16, Greg has his own R1 back, Scott has his own R15 back, and no 2027 pick has moved. npm run verify:picks confirms all 160 slots against four independent sources and calls these two the documented, ruled divergences from the workbook.

theWorkbookNeverCaughtUp.fact: The commissioner's own Sheet1 pick inventory agrees with the board for eight of the ten franchises. The only two it disagrees with are GREG and SCOTT — it still records the pre-contingency position, with Scott holding Greg's 1st and Greg holding Scott's 15th. The workbook was never updated for the contingent leg.
theWorkbookNeverCaughtUp.source: data/draft-pick-inventory-2026-spreadsheet.json against data/smartdraft-room-snapshot.json; asserted by npm run verify:history and npm run verify:picks
theWorkbookNeverCaughtUp.whyFunny: Of ten franchises, the only two the commissioner's spreadsheet has wrong are the two who wrote themselves a contract.

theKeeperClockExploit.headline: The trade did not make Puka Nacua cheap. He was already cheap. What the trade did was bring a dead keeper clock back to life.

priceHistory.event: Drafted by Scott Johnston in ROUND 14, pick 137 of 160.
Kept by Scott at round 12 — his third and final season under the clock.
Priced at round 11 by the ordinary minus-one rule.

theKeeperClockExploit.theRatchet: R14 to R11 in three seasons, entirely by the ordinary rule. Nobody engineered the price. The 2023 draft did.

theRecitalElision.fact: The agreement's own recital describes Nacua as 'drafted in the 12th Round of the 2025 League draft'. In this league a keeper occupies his cost-round slot on the draft sheet, so a keeper and a real pick look identical. Nacua's 'twelfth round' in 2025 was the third rung of a keeper ratchet, not a draft pick — and by then his clock was spent.
theRecitalElision.source: docs/2025-johnston-blome-trade-agreement.pdf recital; data/RECONCILIATION.md, 'Keepers occupy their cost-round slot in these sheets'

theDeadClock.fact: KEEPER LIST for 2025, written before the trade, records Puka Nacua under Scott Johnston with 2024 status '2 of 3', 2025 status '3 of 3' and 2026 status 'N/A'. N/A means he was finished. Scott could not have kept him in 2026 at any price.

theResurrection.fact: KEEPER LIST for 2026, written after the trade, records the same player under Greg Blome with 2025 status '1 of 3', 2026 status '2 of 3', 2027 status '3 of 3', cost round 11, flagged TRADE. The clock the previous year's sheet had marked N/A is back at year one.
theResurrection.whyThisIsTheStory: The commissioner's own two spreadsheets, a year apart, record a keeper clock dying and then being reborn. The mechanism is the league's own rule — 'if a player is traded by a League team, such player's Keeper eligibility restarts with his new League team' — quoted in the recitals of the contract that used it.

whatTheAppRecords.fact: The app REFUSES to state Nacua's clock year. In data/keepers-2026-resolved.json he is the only keeper whose clockYear2026, isFinalKeeperSeason and keepableIn2027 are all null. src/lib/keeper-tenure-dispute.ts records the question with both readings and prints 'Kept in 2026 · final season disputed (2027 or 2028)' on every surface rather than a number.

theTwoReadings.countsFrom: the pre-draft leg that returns him to Scott

whatTheAppRecords.whyFunny: Ten managers, two spreadsheets and a DocuSigned contract all have an answer. The software is the only participant that declines to sign off on it.

thePunchlineNumber.context: The next-biggest keeper bargain on the board is De'Von Achane at +72. Nacua beats the field by 31 picks. He is the fourth-ranked player in the entire pool and he is being taken at the 107th slot of 160.
thePunchlineNumber.method: src/lib/expected-pick.ts — rank the pool by ADP with kept players removed, map the nth-ranked player to the nth draftable slot on this board. Nacua's ADP of 4 is the consensus of nine feeds in data/smartdraft-players.json.

leagueApproval.fact: There is no record anywhere in this repository of the league approving, ratifying, reviewing or vetoing this agreement. The document itself is signed by two people and nobody else — there is no commissioner signature block, no ratification clause, no notice provision and no third party.
leagueApproval.source: docs/2025-johnston-blome-trade-agreement.pdf; searched data/DECISIONS.md, src/lib/governance.ts, src/lib/governance-rules.ts and the full git history

isApprovalEvenRequired.fact: No rule requires it and no rule forbids it. data/DECISIONS.md ballot item 3 puts the question 'Are contingent trades permitted at all?' to the league precisely because 'No rule currently permits or forbids this, which is the problem.'

whatMechanismExisted.fact: ESPN's league settings do provide a 48-hour trade review with 4 veto votes required. But that could only ever have covered the player leg: ESPN holds no draft-pick ownership for an offline draft and has keepers switched off entirely, so the pick legs, the contingency and the keeper consequence existed outside any league system that could review them.

theMediaOutletsTest.fact: The document does not define 'media outlets', does not name a source, does not say who determines the projection, sets no tiebreak, and appoints no adjudicator. The only party with a decision to make under the clause is DHB, who also holds the option.
theMediaOutletsTest.source: docs/2025-johnston-blome-trade-agreement.pdf, clause 2 — by reading, these provisions are absent
theMediaOutletsTest.whyFunny: A clause turning on a majority of media outlets, with nobody appointed to count them.

objectionsOnRecord.fact: One, and it is the operator's. Colin's description of the deal, recorded in data/DECISIONS.md: 'a one-off that should have gone to a vote before it ever happened'. He has also described the arrangement as illegitimate and holds the 2027 reading of the clock. He is a party to the dispute and has no authority over it. Relayed separately on 2026-08-28: 'No one ever agreed to it, no one ever approved it. They just kinda went rogue and did their own damn thing.'

commissionerPosition.fact: Kyle Mertens has NOT ruled on whether the agreement was legitimate. He declined to settle the trade-and-reset loophole unilaterally and sent it to an offseason league vote (ballot item 2), and the contingent-trade question is ballot item 3. What is settled is narrower: Nacua is Scott's at round 11 for 2026, and that rests on the contract's own express term rather than on a quoted ruling from Kyle.
commissionerPosition.source: data/DECISIONS.md, 'Puka Nacua — Scott's, keepable at R11' and ballot items 2 and 3
commissionerPosition.caution: Do not attribute a verbatim ruling on this agreement to Kyle Mertens. None exists in the repo.

theOwnGoal.fact: data/DECISIONS.md notes that the same trade-and-reset mechanism has been used before in this league — 'to hold Trey McBride a third season' — and McBride is COLIN'S keeper, in his third season, showing 3 of 3. Whatever the league decides 'applies retroactively to everyone or to no one'.
theOwnGoal.source: data/DECISIONS.md, ballot item 2; data/spreadsheets keeper lists for 2024, 2025 and 2026
theOwnGoal.whyFunny: The loudest objector to the loophole is holding a keeper he obtained through it.

didItFire.fact: Yes, in every source that matters. The app's board carries Puka Nacua as SCOTT's keeper at 11.07, the live room carries the same, and the 2026 pick ledger shows the netted position — Greg with his own R1 back, Scott with his own R15 back, Scott holding Greg's R3, Greg holding Scott's R16.
didItFire.timing: The contingent leg was due 'on the day before the 2026 League Draft'. The draft is Saturday 2026-08-29, so the due date is Friday 2026-08-28 — the day this was written.
didItFire.source: npm run verify:board-keepers; npm run verify:picks; data/smartdraft-room-snapshot.json
didItFire.caution: The repo holds no record of anyone performing a Friday injury check, and data/DECISIONS.md explicitly asks for one: 'Worth a check on Friday before the board is printed.' Nacua being healthy is assumed by every source here, not verified by any of them. Do not build a joke on his 2026 health status.

skattebo.framing: THE LEGITIMATE VERSION OF THE PLAY. The commissioner's ruling on the comparison, 2026-08-28: 'Nothing compared to the Johnston and Blome trade. Cam Skattebo reached Elbe by trade. It's an art form to keep people high.' Acquiring a player and then keeping him at a good cost round is normal, admired play in this league. Record it as ordinary league business. Do NOT set it beside the Nacua agreement as a lesser scandal — it is not a scandal at all.

trade.source: data/trade-log-2026-spreadsheet.json trade #9; confirmed against the board — Elbe's R4 is Kyle's and Kyle's R8 is Elbe's

whyItIsDifferent.fact: Skattebo's clock was never dead. He was drafted by Kyle Mertens in round 10 of the 2025 draft, pick 95, and the 2026 keeper sheet has him at 2 of 3 — a live, ordinary second season. Kyle could have kept him at round 9 himself and chose two other players instead. Elbe bought an asset that was already keepable. Nothing was resurrected.

keeperBoard2026.note: Every 2026 keeper priced against the RELEASE counterfactual: where this board would have taken him had that one franchise not kept him, everybody else's keepers standing. `slotsSavedByKeeping` is `overall - pickIfReleased`; positive means keeping him cost a later pick than redrafting him would have. This is the KEEPER measure and is NOT comparable to the reach/steal figure on a drafted pick, which is measured against the board that actually existed — see the two-measures note in src/lib/recap-dossier.ts. Derived from the player pool as it stood when this document was written; the recap recomputes from the live pool, so re-pulling ADP can move these by a slot. `npm run verify:recap` reports any drift and `npm run sync:history-keepers` closes it.
keeperBoard2026.source: npm run verify:board-keepers for slots and owners; steal derived from data/smartdraft-players.json via the method in src/lib/expected-pick.ts

keeperCounterfactual.note: Who each franchise COULD have kept, and at what derived cost round. Cost rounds come from data/keeper-eligibility-2026.json's roundToKeep2026 column, which implements 'last season's round minus one, or round 9 for a free-agent acquisition'. Players pricing to round 0 are barred outright by the round-1 ruling. A player is only actually keepable if his franchise also OWNS a pick in the cost round — several do not, and that is where the good material is.
keeperCounterfactual.source: data/keeper-eligibility-2026.json cross-referenced against pick ownership in data/smartdraft-room-snapshot.json

NOBODY KEPT A PLAYER AT AN OBVIOUSLY BAD PRICE EITHER. The worst value on the board is +4 picks, which is still a bargain. There is no keeper in this league that anyone overpaid for.

otherOddities.fact: The league's keeper rules exist in writing in exactly one place: the recitals of a private contract between two managers. This app derives its rules from that document.
otherOddities.source: docs/2025-johnston-blome-trade-agreement.pdf; data/DECISIONS.md, 'Primary source: the Johnston/Blome trade agreement'

otherOddities.fact: ESPN has had the keeper feature switched OFF for at least five straight seasons, and ESPN structurally cannot represent a keeper clock at all. This app has to be the system of record for keepers; ESPN will never be able to hold them.

The draft order is not derivable from standings even in principle, because it is the record of ten free choices in a slot auction. Any code that computes an order from standings is wrong by construction.

A free-agent convention change in the 2026 keeper sheet silently repriced 75 free agents by one round — the 2024 and 2025 sheets wrote the literal string 'FA' and priced at R9, while the 2026 sheet wrote the number 9 and the minus-one formula turned it into R8. It changed exactly one actual keeper: Colston Loveland, ruled back to R9.
otherOddities.source: data/RECONCILIATION.md, 'How cost rounds are derived'; data/DECISIONS.md

otherOddities.fact: Ten managers each held a round-1 player going into 2026 and not one declared him. The round-1 ineligibility ruling therefore codified existing practice rather than introducing a rule — and it changed nothing on this board.
otherOddities.source: data/DECISIONS.md, 'First-round picks can NEVER be kept'; npm run verify:round1

otherOddities.fact: A round-2 keeper now gets ONE keeper season instead of two — an accident of two rules that were each decided on their own merits colliding. Nobody chose it, nobody has ever been affected by it, and the commissioner declined to rule on it.

The keeper cost basis carries across a trade while the clock resets, so a player can in principle be passed around and held indefinitely at an ever-cheaper round until the formula reaches zero. That is the rule as written.

There is a broken external link in the workbook pointing at a file on a law firm's network share, with cached sheet names 'DHB Sandmen', 'BChen Overall', 'BChen QB', 'BChen TE'. That was the league's old rankings source and it is not in this repo.
Nobody in this league is a committed fan of any single NFL team, so jokes about somebody stacking their favourite franchise do not land.

unverified.state: The operator has stated it is Scott JOHNSTON. Nothing in the repository establishes it.
